newsitem.title: GERMANY: Arthuis stresses France aims to keep deficits low.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis stresses France aims to keep deficits low.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis on Friday stressed that France intended to achieve long-term fiscal stability, adding that such discipline will be essential for the stability of the future European currency.

In a speech prepared for delivery to the European Banking Congress in Frankfurt, Arthuis said the French budget deficit would be within the three percent limit compared to total output, as stated in the Maastricht Treaty, in 1997.
France then intended to continue to consolidate its budgets, he added, saying that the deficit would be reduced to 2.8 percent in 1998 and below two percent by the year 2001.

Countries which want to participate in the European currency from the start in 1999 must meet certain economic goals in 1997. Most countries have faced the greatest difficulty in meeting the fiscal targets.
